note: Phase 10B Section 12: quality bar applied per format, using Q8 as reference and Q4 as the known bad-quality extreme (Phase 10A). Source: multi_prompt_aggregate.json (5 prompts x 2 models, the more robust signal) plus the single-prompt/long-generation ladders for corroboration.
bar: A Q5 candidate is promising only if: clearly better than Q4 on top1, clearly better than Q4 on rel-L2, clearly better than Q4 on NLL, memory meaningfully lower than Q8, no severe instability across prompts.

q5_0.vs_q4_top1: 135M: marginal (93.1% vs 92.5% mean) -- NOT clearly better on this model. 360M: clearly better (98.6% vs 96.5% mean).
q5_0.vs_q4_rel_l2: Clearly better on both models (135M: 0.065 vs 0.113, ~42% lower; 360M: 0.056 vs 0.116, ~52% lower).
q5_0.vs_q4_nll: Clearly better on both models (135M: 0.0003 vs 0.0249; 360M: 0.0076 vs 0.0151) -- though delta_nll's sign flips per-prompt at n=5, so this signal is noisier than top1/rel_l2.
q5_0.memory_vs_q8: 34.375% of native vs Q8's 53.125% -- 64.7% of Q8's footprint, a real ~35% additional reduction vs Q8.
q5_0.stability: Worst-case prompt on 135M (simple_reasoning, top1=78.6%) is WORSE than Q4's own worst case (87.5%) on the same model -- a real, not-hidden caveat. 360M worst case (96.1%) is comfortably clear of Q4's (94.5%).
q5_0.verdict: Promising on the larger model, but the smallest-model worst-case top1 result does not clear the bar cleanly -- mixed.

q5_1.vs_q4_top1: Clearly better on both models (135M: 94.5% vs 92.5%; 360M: 98.65% vs 96.5%).
q5_1.vs_q4_rel_l2: Clearly better on both models (135M: 0.052 vs 0.113, ~54% lower; 360M: 0.049 vs 0.116, ~58% lower) -- the best rel-L2 of any Q5 variant, on both models.
q5_1.vs_q4_nll: Clearly better on both models by mean, and the more consistent of the two Q5 variants (same noisy-sign caveat as q5_0 applies).
q5_1.memory_vs_q8: 37.5% of native vs Q8's 53.125% -- 70.6% of Q8's footprint, a real ~29% additional reduction vs Q8 (costs ~9% more bytes than q5_0 for the quality gain below).
q5_1.stability: Worst-case prompt on 135M (simple_reasoning, top1=85.7%) is close to but still slightly below Q4's own worst case (87.5%) -- the same caveat as q5_0, milder. 360M worst case (96.9%) is comfortably clear of Q4's.
q5_1.verdict: Consistently the stronger of the two Q5 variants across every prompt-level metric (top1, rel-L2, worst-case) on both models, at a modest memory cost over q5_0.

cross_format_comparison.memory: q5_0 < q5_1 (smaller) -- 34.375% vs 37.5% of native, q5_0 costs about 9% fewer bytes than q5_1
cross_format_comparison.conclusion: q5_1 wins on every quality axis measured, consistently, on both models -- q5_0's only advantage is a modest (~9%) additional memory saving. Given the phase's mandate to find a format 'whose quality stays much closer to Q8 than Q4', quality is weighted over the marginal extra memory saving here.
